finding.claim: Host key is trusted by default: CanTrustHostKey returns true when no HostKeyReceived handler exists, and HostKeyEventArgs.CanTrust defaults to true, so a consumer handler that does not explicitly reject the key also accepts it. No known_hosts, pinning, or fingerprint check exists in the library.
finding.source: Network peer's host key and signature in SSH_MSG_KEXDH_REPLY (attacker controls them in a MITM position or as a malicious server)
finding.sink: Session accepts the server identity and proceeds to authentication, so password/key auth material is sent to the attacker-controlled peer

trace.note: _hostKey = message.HostKey and _signature = message.Signature taken from the wire
Finish() after shared secret computed
ValidateExchangeHash() called
VerifySignature(exchangeHash, sig) && CanTrustHostKey(keyAlgorithm)
handlers = HostKeyReceived; if null, falls through to return true at 478
CanTrust = true in constructor, so a handler that never sets it also trusts
BaseClient subscribes Session_HostKeyReceived, which only forwards to the user event; the default-true still applies

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification over the exchange hash (KeyExchange.cs:493) proves possession of the presented key only, not identity. No known_hosts, fingerprint pinning, or default-deny exists. The consumer-supplied handler is the only control and is opt-in.

finding.claim: The port-only ForwardedPortDynamic(uint port) constructor leaves BoundHost empty, so the SOCKS listener binds IPAddress.Any and accepts SOCKS4/SOCKS5 requests from any network peer with no authentication, relaying through the SSH session.
finding.source: Any network peer that can reach the listening port (remote, unauthenticated)
finding.sink: SSH direct-tcpip tunnel opened to a destination chosen by the SOCKS client, using the client's SSH identity (pivot into networks reachable from the SSH server)

trace.note: ForwardedPortDynamic(uint port) calls this(string.Empty, port)
BoundHost = host (empty)
ip = IPAddress.Any when BoundHost is empty
IPEndPoint(ip, port); listener bound to all interfaces
SOCKS4 path reads a user id and replies with 0x00 (granted) without checking it
SOCKS5 method selection: if client offers method 0x00 (no auth)
replies {0x05,0x00} (no auth accepted) with no credential check

finding.guards_checked: No SOCKS authentication is enforced on either protocol path. The only control is that the listener is started explicitly by the caller. I did not trace the downstream direct-tcpip channel-open path or any destination allow-listing.

finding.claim: The default SCP remote-path transformation (DoubleQuote) escapes only the double-quote character. A path containing $(...) or backticks is interpolated into the remote exec command and executed by the server's shell.
finding.source: Path string supplied by the calling application (attacker-controlled if the app builds remote paths from untrusted input)
finding.sink: channel.SendExecRequest on the remote SSH server, executed by the remote shell

trace.note: DefaultTransform returns RemotePathTransformation.DoubleQuote
public ctors pass DefaultTransform when no transform is specified
Transform: wraps in quotes; only '"' gets a backslash prefix; $ ` and \ are left unescaped
upload: $"scp -t ... {Transform(posixPath.Directory)}" concatenated into exec string
download: string.Concat("scp -f ", Transform(filename)) sent as exec request

finding.guards_checked: Double-quote escaping of '"' only. Not escaped: '$', backtick, and '\' (a trailing backslash can also break out of the quotes). A safer ShellQuote transformation exists (RemotePathShellQuoteTransformation) but is not the default.

finding.claim: SCP upload builds C and D protocol records from local file and directory names with no sanitization. A name containing LF (legal on POSIX) breaks record framing, so an uploaded tree from an untrusted source can desynchronize the SCP stream. Exploitability is not confirmed.
finding.source: Local file or directory name in a tree being uploaded (attacker-controlled if the app uploads an untrusted directory, e.g. extracted from an archive)
finding.sink: SCP protocol stream read by the remote 'scp -t' sink

trace.note: UploadDirectoryContent passes file.Name unvalidated
UploadFileModeAndName: string.Format("C0644 {0} {1}\n", size, serverFileName)
directory.Name passed unvalidated
UploadDirectoryModeAndName: string.Format("D0755 0 {0}\n", directoryName)
EnsureValidLocalName exists but is only called on download (lines 930, 961), never on upload

finding.guards_checked: None on the upload side. The download side validates names with EnsureValidLocalName (ScpClient.cs:840-854), which rejects separators and '.'/'..' but is not applied to outgoing names. The LF injection path is unverified; the injected header may be consumed as file content rather than as a command.

finding.claim: The HTTP CONNECT request line interpolates connectionInfo.Host without rejecting CR/LF, so a host string containing CRLF injects arbitrary headers or request lines into the proxy request.
finding.source: connectionInfo.Host value (attacker-controlled only if the app derives the target host from untrusted input)
finding.sink: Plaintext HTTP request written to the proxy socket

trace.note: SocketAbstraction.Send of string.Format("CONNECT {0}:{1} HTTP/1.0\r\n", Host, Port)
connectionInfo.Host inserted with no validation

finding.guards_checked: No CR/LF or character validation on the host. Proxy credentials are base64-encoded (HttpConnector.cs:71), so they are not injectable. Impact is limited to the proxy request.

finding.claim: A malicious or MITM proxy can set Content-Length up to int.MaxValue; the client allocates that buffer and reads it before the connection proceeds, causing a large per-connection memory allocation.
finding.source: Content-Length header from the proxy response (HttpConnector.cs:112)

trace.note: contentLength = int.Parse(fieldValue) with no upper bound
if (contentLength > 0)
new byte[contentLength] allocated up to ~2 GiB

finding.guards_checked: Only contentLength > 0 and the socket read timeout (line 125). No cap on size. Impact is client memory exhaustion under a hostile proxy.

finding.claim: The server's DH public value f and, for group exchange, the server-chosen safe prime are used without range or size checks. The client accepts any server-chosen group, and the minimum group size is only 2x hash bits.
finding.source: SSH_MSG_KEXDH_REPLY f value (KeyExchangeDiffieHellman.cs:126) and SSH_MSG_KEX_DH_GEX_GROUP prime (KeyExchangeDiffieHellmanGroupExchange.cs:162)
finding.sink: DHBasicAgreement shared-secret computation and client ephemeral key generation over a server-chosen group

trace.note: _serverExchangeValue = message.F; no 1 < f < p-1 check
DHPublicKeyParameters built from F with no validation
_prime = groupMessage.SafePrimeBytes; no check against requested min/max or primality
minimumBitLength = 2 * _hashLengthInBits (RFC 4419 ss. 6.2 recommends checking requested bounds)

finding.guards_checked: Exchange-hash signature verification (indirect, after shared secret is computed) and host key trust (which F1 weakens). Whether BouncyCastle's DHBasicAgreement rejects f values was not verified. Impact is weak-group exposure of the client's ephemeral exponent to a malicious server.

finding.claim: SFTP framing reads a signed Int32 length from the server and only checks data.Count - 4 < packetLength, so a negative length passes the guard and Slice throws. The SSH path similarly does not validate paddingLength against packetLength. Both produce an exception that tears down the affected session rather than crashing the process.
finding.source: Length field in a server SFTP packet (SftpSession.cs:266/306) or SSH padding byte (Session.cs:1414)
finding.sink: ArraySegment.Slice / ArraySegment ctor with negative count (SftpSession.cs:273, 316; Session.cs:1416-1419)

trace.note: packetLength = ReadInt32BigEndian(data), may be negative
guard data.Count - 4 < packetLength is false for negative values
data.Slice(4, packetLength) with negative count throws
OnDataReceived called inside try
catch -> RaiseError(ex)
paddingLength read from packet; payload count = packetLength - paddingLength - 1 with no bound check

finding.guards_checked: Bounds check on packetLength for SSH (Session.cs:1308) and data.Count-based guard for SFTP. Exceptions are caught in SubsystemSession.cs:212-221 and Channel.cs:651-658, so this is availability impact only (session error, not process crash).
